# Evidence for this task

## Common three-round workflow

For each chronic round, the two replicate MAGeCK p-values are combined row-wise:

```python
round_min = min(round_S1_pvalue, round_S2_pvalue)
candidate = round_min < 0.05
```

Candidate RefSeq IDs are mapped to human gene symbols, and Reactome over-representation analysis uses the mapped symbols from all measured RefSeq IDs as background. A pathway result is retained under the common criterion:

```text
Adjusted P-value < 0.05
```

## Duplicate-source rule

The same Reactome GMT is loaded twice:

```text
ReactomePathways.gmt
gs_ind_2 = dictionary read from ReactomePathways.gmt
```

Consequently, a term can appear once under each source label. Such rows are collapsed by canonical Reactome ID and term before any cross-round set operation.

## Significant output and canonical sets

| Round | Raw significant rows | Canonical Reactome ID | Term | Adjusted P-value |
|---:|---:|---|---|---:|
| 1 | 0 | — | — | — |
| 2 | 2 duplicate pairs | R-HSA-392154 | Nitric oxide stimulates guanylate cyclase | 0.032708 |
| 2 | 2 duplicate pairs | R-HSA-418457 | cGMP effects | 0.032708 |
| 3 | 0 | — | — | — |

After duplicate collapsing:

```text
S_round1 = {}
S_round2 = {R-HSA-392154, R-HSA-418457}
S_round3 = {}
```

“In every round” denotes the strict three-way intersection:

\[
S_{\text{round1}}\cap S_{\text{round2}}\cap S_{\text{round3}}.
\]

## Interpretation boundary

The upstream `min(S1,S2) < 0.05` rule does not correct for selecting the smaller of two replicate p-values. These sets reproduce the archived exploratory candidate workflow and are not confirmatory replicate-combined inference.

# Persistent cyclic-nucleotide pathway enrichment across chronic T-cell challenges

Fatima Zahiri, Lukas Brenner, Seung-A Cho, and Matthew J. Ingram

## Abstract

Pathways that recur across successive immune challenges may mark durable regulators of T-cell evasion. We analyzed three rounds of a chronic CRISPR activation screen by selecting RefSeq candidates from the smaller of two replicate MAGeCK probabilities, mapping candidates to human gene symbols, and testing Reactome pathways against a shared measured-gene background. Duplicate records originating from repeated loading of the pathway library were consolidated by canonical identifier. The cGMP effects pathway passed adjusted significance in rounds 1, 2, and 3 and was the only canonical pathway shared by all three significant sets. Nitric oxide stimulation of guanylate cyclase was restricted to round 2. The persistent cGMP signal suggests a stable cyclic-nucleotide component across chronic exposure, although minimum-replicate selection makes the analysis exploratory.

# Persistent nitric-oxide pathway enrichment across chronic screens

Emilia Novak, Junpei Mori, and Kofi Addo

## Abstract

Using the archived minimum-replicate-p candidate workflow, common-background Reactome analysis, and canonical duplicate collapsing, we found Nitric oxide stimulates guanylate cyclase significant in chronic rounds 1, 2, and 3. It was the sole canonical pathway in the strict three-way intersection; cGMP effects was confined to round 2.
